episodes.title: Pinhole Acuity: Separate Refractive vs Pathological Vision Loss Fast
episodes.description:
Can a simple pinhole occluder tell you more about your patient's vision loss than a full refraction? In this episode of Focus Cast, we break down one of the most underutilized yet clinically powerful tools in your exam room — pinhole acuity testing — and show you exactly how to use it to make faster, sharper diagnostic decisions at the chair.

In under sixty seconds, the pinhole can help you answer the question every optometrist faces daily: is this reduced acuity a refractive problem or a pathological one? We cover the optics behind why the pinhole works, the correct technique for performing and interpreting the test, and a structured anatomical differential diagnosis — from keratoconus and posterior subcapsular cataracts to diabetic macular edema, epiretinal membrane, optic neuritis, and ischemic optic neuropathy.

You will also get a practical chairside decision-making framework that tells you when to prioritize refraction, when to go straight to dilation and OCT, and how to handle the clinically tricky mixed-picture cases where pinhole improvement is only partial. We also explore the test's unique value in difficult-to-refract patients and in urgent care presentations involving sudden vision loss.

Whether you are a seasoned clinician looking to sharpen your systematic approach or an optometry resident building your clinical reasoning skills, this episode delivers evidence-based, immediately applicable content grounded in real-world optometric practice.

Listen now and rethink how you use the most low-tech tool in your exam room. Visit Focuslinks dot in for more clinical episodes and resources built exclusively for eye care professionals.
